topics.title: Humanity
topics.short: Each prosthetic costs humanity. Below 70 a survivor's mood is capped; below 50 they are detached and their partner and children suffer.
topics.long:
Humanity starts at 100 and drops by a fixed cost for every prosthetic fitted (crude parts cost nothing). It never comes back while the part is on. The breakdown below shows each part's cost for the selected survivor.

## Effects

- **Below 70**: mood is capped at 40 + 60 × humanity / 70. At 50 that is about 83, at 35 it is 70, at 0 it is 40.
- **Below 50, detached**: their partner's bond erodes every hour, faster the lower humanity is, and the couple may split. Their children's mood is capped at 70. Odd lines start appearing in the log.

## Costs per part

- Crude 0, Mechanical 3, Powered 8, Cyborg 15, Network-grade 22.
- Replacing a **healthy** limb by choice (Cyborg or better, adults only) costs more: 35 or 45.
- The Linked "Calm" injector also costs humanity.

## Tips

- Two Cyborg legs and an arm put someone at 55: fine. One elective Network-grade implant more and they are detached.
- Keep heavy cyborgs single or with a patient partner.

topics.title: Prosthetics and surgery
topics.short: Five tiers, from strapped-on Crude parts to Network-grade implants. Higher tiers beat flesh but need surgery, upkeep and humanity.
topics.long:
A lost limb can be replaced, and from Cyborg tier a healthy one too.

## Tiers

- **Crude** (T0): wood and scrap, strapped on at Med Bay 1. Worse than the original.
- **Mechanical** (T1): strapped on, no upkeep. 3 humanity.
- **Powered** (T2): surgery at Med Bay 2; can specialise. Service every 10 days. 8 humanity.
- **Cyborg** (T3): surgery by a Cyber-Surgeon; better than flesh. 15 humanity (35 elective).
- **Network-grade** (T4): Med Bay 3, built from Linked cores; the best, but Linked within 6 tiles can lock it up, 15% each, up to 60% a round. 22 humanity (45 elective).

## Surgery

The patient holds a bed while the medic works. The chance starts at 75%, less for higher tiers, plus the medic's skill, surgical kits and perks, between 30% and 97%. A failure still fits the part but leaves an infection.

## Upkeep

Powered parts and up need a service (scrap and electronics) every few days; missed, the part loses efficiency, down to 60%.

## Specialisations

Arms (Labor, Precision, Hacker, Blade, Gun), legs (Runner, Jumper, Silent, Armored) and eyes. A matching pair adds a set bonus. Open the tree from the Med Bay.

topics.title: Crafting and quality
topics.short: Production buildings work a queue of orders. Gear rolls Crude, Standard or Fine from the best worker's skill and the building level.
topics.long:
Workshop, Tailor, Kitchen, Armory, Electronics Lab, Garage and Med Bay all make things the same way.

## The queue

- Each building holds up to 8 orders: a count, or **repeat** forever. It works one at a time.
- An order is paid when it starts. Cancelling refunds a paid batch.
- If no worker has the skill an order needs, workers **practise** and the panel says how long until someone is ready.

## Quality

Gear, mods, vehicle parts, supplies and dishes roll a quality when made:

- Score = best worker's skill / 100 + 0.05 per building level above 1, give or take 0.2 at random, plus perk bonuses.
- At 0.6 or more it is **Fine** (×1.25 stats, ×0.9 weight); at 0.15 or more **Standard**; below that **Crude** (×0.8 stats, ×1.15 weight).
- The recipe panel shows the odds for your current crew.

## Tips

- One skilled worker sets the quality for the whole building: put your best crafter there.
- Upgrading a building raises both speed and quality.

topics.title: Schematics
topics.short: Schematics are knowledge: they unlock recipes, building levels, perks, vehicles and prosthetic tiers. Find them, decrypt them, trade or research them.
topics.long:
Most basic recipes and buildings are open from the start. Everything else needs its **schematic**.

## Where they come from

- **Loot**: caches and lockers roll for one, more often in dangerous zones. Hacked **terminals** are the best source.
- **Kills**: the Linked sometimes carry one; Wardens often do.
- **Trade**: a trader at the Radio Mast sells them (see [[trading]]).
- **Research** at the Town Hall (see [[research]]).
- Story missions.

## Encrypted chips

Some arrive as an encrypted chip. Queue its **Decrypt** order at the Electronics Lab (level 2, level 3 for tier 4) with a worker of Electronics 20 or more.

## Heard of

A schematic you saw but did not bring home, such as one a failed hack showed you, is marked **heard of**. Only heard-of schematics can be researched.

## Duplicates

A copy of one you know becomes Research Data. You can also make copies to trade.

## Tips

- Open the archive with **I** (Items → Schematics) to see what is known, waiting, heard of or unknown.

topics.title: Research
topics.short: Research a schematic you have heard of at the Town Hall, paying Research Data. Tier 1–2 need Town Hall 2, tier 3 Town Hall 3 and a Lab 2.
topics.long:
Research turns a schematic you have **heard of** into one you know, so bad luck with loot never locks you out. It happens at the Town Hall, one project at a time.

## Requirements

- Tiers 1 and 2: Town Hall level 2. Tier 3: Town Hall level 3 and an Electronics Lab level 2.
- Cost: 4, 8 or 16 Research Data by tier, paid at the start.
- Tier 4 schematics cannot be researched: they come from the Black Grid, Wardens or the story.

## The researcher

Pick an adult; they leave their job while researching and work on the day shift. Speed grows with their **Intellect** and **Electronics** skill.

## Research Data

- A duplicate schematic turns into Research Data.
- Salvage a chip you do not need into Research Data.
- Taking electronics apart sometimes yields one (see [[electronics]]).
- The trader buys and sells it.

## Tips

- Use a high-Intellect survivor who is not your best worker anywhere else.

topics.title: Power
topics.short: Generators, solar arrays and battery banks feed the Lab, Med Bay, charging bench and Floodlights. Over capacity, things brown out.
topics.long:
Nothing needs power to work at all; power makes some buildings better. Until you build a generator or bank, nothing changes. Press **P** for the power overlay.

## Supply

- **Fuel Generator**: 6, 9 or 12 power by level; burns fuel, or wood if out of fuel.
- **Solar Array**: 3, 5 or 8 at full sun; less at dawn and dusk, nothing at night, less under cloud.
- **Battery Bank**: stores 30, 60 or 100 and releases it at a limited rate.

## What uses it

- **Electronics Lab**: +25% crafting speed; tier 3 parts need it.
- **Med Bay** level 3: +5% surgery success.
- **Charging bench**: charges devices 5× faster.
- **Floodlights**: +15% night-shift output.
- The Radio Mast and Cold Cellar draw power too, and defenses near a powered building get a bonus.

Consumers only draw while their crew is on shift.

## Overload

If demand is over supply, the last consumers in line are cut (a brownout). Asking for far more than you have for hours trips the breaker for a while. Switch buildings off the grid in their panel.

topics.title: Electronics and devices
topics.short: The Electronics Lab turns scrap into components, then devices: scanners, jammers, radios, EMPs, decoys and drones. Old gadgets come apart for parts.
topics.long:
## Components

The Lab builds a chain: scrap → wiring → circuit boards → antennas and sensor modules. Microchips and cyan **Network chips** (from Linked circuitry) are tier 3 and need [[power]].

## Devices

- **Scanner**: sees hostiles nearby through walls and stealth. **Jammer**: cuts the Linked off their Network nearby.
- **Radios**: two on a side add aim within range and extra [[pings]].
- **EMP**: knocks out Linked, drones and cameras nearby (and Network-grade implants, yours too).
- **Holo-decoy** and **noise decoy**: lure enemies.
- Sensor kits, rangefinders and drones (see [[drones]]).

Quality scales a device's radius, battery, hack chance or range (see [[crafting]]).

## Charges

Some devices have charges. They come home drained and wait on the charging bench; power makes it 5× faster.

## Disassembly

Broken gadgets, dead radios and smashed drones from loot can be taken apart at the Lab for components, sometimes with a Research Data. Electronics skill raises the yield.

## Tips

- Lab work also trains Hacking and Drone Piloting.

topics.title: Gear mods and Mk upgrades
topics.short: Fit sights, grips, plating and linings into gear slots at the Armory, Workshop or Tailor. A Mk II or III kit adds slots and stats.
topics.long:
Weapons, armor, clothing and helmets have **mod slots**. A firearm takes sight, muzzle, stock and underbarrel mods; melee weapons edge, grip and coil; armor plating, lining, outer layer and webbing.

## Fitting

- Open the **Gear Bench** from the production panel of an Armory, Workshop or Tailor.
- Fitting into a full slot swaps the old mod out; removing a mod returns it intact.
- The compare column shows the build before and after.

## Mk upgrades

- Mk I has one slot, Mk II two, Mk III three.
- A **Mk kit** of the gear's family is fitted at the Armory or Tailor, one Mk at a time.
- Mk II adds ×1.08 damage and +2% accuracy to weapons, more armor and coverage to worn gear. Mk III ×1.16 and +4%.

## Quality

Mods roll a quality like any crafted item: a Fine mod's benefits are ×1.25 and its drawbacks smaller.

## In the field

With the Jury-rig perk a survivor can fit or remove a mod for 1 AP. A ranged shot after moving loses some accuracy; a stock takes part of that off.
